questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The only thing I knew was that I wanted it to be within Europe, therefore I applied to universities in Europe I had the option of applying to.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, and if we had questions there were a lot of people we could write to via e-mail and get help from them.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a large gathering for all exchange students at the faculty of social science where we got all the important information. And they updates us via e-mail with deadline etc. we should remember.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We struggled quite a lot to find housing but a good idea is to start looking a good amount of time in advance. We ended up getting housing through AirBnB.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus or not living in the dorms can maybe be a bit more lonely because the people living together at the dorms have a lot of social things happening. But, you could also find roomates to live with, that was what I did. But I would say it depends on what kind of person you are, if you are very social you could go for the dorms (and don't mind a little bacteria), and if you need you own time to recarge maybe go for private housing or at least a one person room at the dorm if possible.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very confusing and I personally got a little dissapointed because many of the courses that was pre-approved did not even exsist in my semester or else the spots would be filled so quick. It is very important to be prepared with the course codes on the day of course registration because you need to search for the course with that. So be prepared for not getting all of the courses you wanted and to do a new pre approval.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You needed to go onto the university system side, and then you could search for the subjects. You need all of the course codes, which can be found in the course catalogue. And then you can choose the ones you want, but there is no guarantee that youl will get a spot or that the course is provided in your semester. A tip is to search for the courses you want to attend the most first, so the spots do not get filled before you search it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We of course got information of how we should do on the registration day, and I believe it was recorded and uploaded to us as well. But on the day we were on our own.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very succesfull, a lot of the ones I wanted was not provided in my semester. I only ended up getting two of the courses I wanted out of five.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The situation can be a bit stressful and disapointing (at least it was for me), but try to keep calm and contact the teachers and attend the courses you have registrated for too see which ones you like the most. But in the end I found courses that were interested and linked up with the amount of ETCS points I needed, so you most likely will too.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I had mainly BA courses, and then one MA course. 
For me the MA course was very good and interesting, and not to hard to follow.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
In terms of lectures it was pretty much the same, just the professor lecturing and then we could ask questions during the lecture if we wanted too. 
In the seminars it was a bit different, where the exercises were done in plenum and at home we get to do the exercises on our own and in groups and maybe discuss them afterwards.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Contemporary crises and social-ecological transformation
Principles of Economics 
Advanced Data Analysis in MS Excel
Topics in Industrial Organization 
International Trade
Energy Security in Israel and the Middle East

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would really recommend: 
Contemporary crises and social-ecological transformation - as it was very interesting and we got to do a group project of our own choosing which was quite nice. 
Advanced Data Analysis in MS Excel - if you want to learn how to use Excel and different functions I would recommend this. I got a lot out of it. 
Energy Security in Israel and the Middle East - this course was also very interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really anything unexpected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food were less expensive, but my rent were a lot higher than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different things were available, you enroll in different sport activities, and there were also held a lot of MSN events you could sign up to, to meet other exchange students (for example, pub quizzes, international dinners, game nights etc.)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to sign up for some of the different MSN events, depending on what you would like to attend. It was a great way to meet new exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to just enjoy the city and explore it on the days off. In the weekends it is fun to visit other cities in Prague, for example, Karlovy Vary or Brno. Also, the national museuem was a quite nice experience. Or else just go out and have fun with the other exchange students.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It would say it was quite easy, I did not feel like there were a major difference.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: In my experience we did not really meet that many local students, and if we had classes with them they mostly kept to themselves. But maybe you could ask them for advice or what they would recommend as locals in the city.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The only thing was that the elderly population could not speak english, so that could be a barrier, but otherwise there wasn't really much of a difference.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The locals were always very nice to speak too. Also the city was just beautiful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared with the course codes before the course registration starts. 
Enjoy and explore the city as much as possible. 
Try to get to know other people than from your own country.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Don't feel stupid for asking questions to your coordinators, they are there too help you. 
And also it could be a good idea to get a "buddy".

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience something new, it was fun trying to live in another country and studying there.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing the people at home, but they will still be there when you get back.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
